'''''Euphorbia stygiana''''' ([[Portuguese Language|Portuguese]]: '''''Trovisco-macho''''') is a species of [[evergreen]] shrub in the family [[Euphorbiaceae]], [[endemic]] to several islands of the [[Azores]]. It has a [[critically endangered]] [[subspecies]] (subsp. ''santamariae'') with only 20 known remaining mature individuals in the wild.

==Description==
''Euphorbia stygiana'' is an evergreen shrub with low but robust [[Serpentine shape|serpentine]], green stems; white-veined, thick, leathery blue-dark green leaves and large yellow-green flower heads which are strongly honey-scented in spring and summer (from May to June). It can grow up to about {{convert|10|m|ft}} tall in its native environment but is often {{convert|1.5|m|ft}} tall and spreads to about {{convert|1.5|m|ft}} wide.<ref name="tropical">{{cite web |title=Euphorbia stygiana |url=https://www.turn-it-tropical.co.uk/product/euphorbia-stygiana-plug-plant/ |publisher=turn-it-tropical.co.uk |access-date=1 December 2020}}</ref><ref name="panglobal">{{cite web |title=Euphorbia stygiana |url=http://www.panglobalplants.com/plants-for-sale/exotics/E/1/ |publisher=panglobalplants.com |access-date=1 December 2020}}</ref><ref name="dave">{{cite web |title=Euphorbia Species: Euphorbia stygiana |url=https://davesgarden.com/guides/pf/go/168761/#b |publisher=davesgarden.com |access-date=1 December 2020}}</ref>

The leaves are {{convert|7|-|14|x|1.5|-|3.5|cm|in}} long, slightly [[pubescent (botany)|pubescent]] on the bottom side. The fruits are {{convert|5|-|7|mm|in}}, striated, subglobous and warty.<ref name="Natura">{{cite web |title=Euphorbia stygiana Watson |url=http://redenatura2000.azores.gov.pt/Web01/fichas/flora/euphorbia_stygiana.htm |publisher=[[Natura 2000|Natura 2000 Azores]] |access-date=1 December 2020}}</ref>  During cold winters (especially outside its native range) these leaves may turn to a brilliant crimson colour.<ref>{{cite web |title=Euphorbia stygiana |url=https://www.rightplants4me.co.uk/plant/2003 |publisher=rightplants4me.co.uk |access-date=1 December 2020}}</ref>

It is hardy down to [[Hardiness zone|USDA]] Zone 8b: to {{convert|-9.4|C|F}} and can be propagated through stem cuttings.<ref name="dave" />

==Distribution and habitat==
''Euphorbia stygiana'' is endemic to all [[Azorean]] islands except [[Graciosa]] where it inhabits the extremely humid highlands of the archipelago from {{convert|300|to|1100|m|ft}} in altitude, especially on [[Pico Island]], in sheltered places such as ravines, craters and dense [[Laurisilva|laurel]]-[[Juniperus brevifolia|Juniperus]] forests.<ref name="Natura" /><ref>{{cite web |title=Euphorbia stygiana H.C.Watson |url=https://acores.flora-on.pt/#/1euphorbia+stygiana |publisher=Flora-on |access-date=1 December 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Euphorbia stygiana Watson (EUPHORBIACEAE) - Trovisco-macho |url=http://siaram.azores.gov.pt/flora/flora-vascular/trovisco/1.html |publisher=siaram.azores.gov.pt |access-date=1 December 2020}}</ref>

==Subspecies==
[[File:Euphorbia stygiana - Botanischer Garten, Frankfurt am Main - DSC03147.JPG|thumb|left|Specimen at the [[Botanical Garden Frankfurt|Frankfurt Botanical Garden]]]]
There are two known subspecies: 

*'''''subsp. santamariae''''' – a [[critically endangered]] subspecies native only to the island of [[Santa Maria Island|Santa Maria]] with less than 20 known mature individuals remaining in the wild, restricted to {{convert|343|sqkm|sqmi}}. The remaining population rests in a steep slope of a valley embedded in a stream, in a humid forest dominated by ''[[Pittosporum undulatum]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=''Euphorbia stygiana'' subsp. ''santamariae'' H.Schaef. |url=https://acores.flora-on.pt/#/0-yIx |publisher=Flora-on |access-date=1 December 2020}}</ref> It is a smaller tree, and has a strong [[apical dominance]]. Foliage is less leathery with a faint bluish bloom.<ref name="panglobal" /> It also has a less pronounced [[leaf vein]] and has fuzzy inflorescences with orange [[extrafloral nectaries]].<ref>{{cite web |title=O trovisco-macho mais raro da Europa |url=https://dias-com-arvores.blogspot.com/2018/06/o-trovisco-macho-mais-raro-da-europa.html |publisher=Paulo V. Araújo, Maria P. Carvalho |access-date=1 December 2020}}</ref>

*'''''subsp. stygiana''''' – the most common subspecies, inhabiting most of the Azorean islands except [[Graciosa Island|Graciosa]] and [[Santa Maria Island|Santa Maria]] in high altitude, humid [[Laurisilva|laurel]]-[[Juniperus brevifolia|Juniperus]] forests.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://acores.flora-on.pt/#/1Euphorbia+stygiana |title=Euphorbia stygiana |publisher=Flora-on |access-date=September 2, 2020}}</ref>

==Threats==
The species is mainly threatened by agricultural development, change in land use, and invasive species and the subsequent increase in competition.<ref name="IUCN">{{cite web |title=Euphorbia stygiana subsp. santamariae |url=https://www.iucnredlist.org/species/162422/120954821 |publisher=[[IUCN]] |access-date=1 December 2020}}</ref>

==Toxicity==
Like other members of the ''[[Euphorbia]]'' genus, ''E. stygiana'' has a milky white [[sap]] that may cause skin irritation or allergic reaction when in contact with the skin or eye.<ref name="dave" /> It is [[toxic]] if eaten.<ref name="tropical" />
